notes: Context: NyxForge builds a VS Code extension (Nyx Assist) used by ~120 internal + beta users. Goal: low-latency inline completions and streaming block completions with stable model outputs.
Initial ask: <50ms inline suggestion latency target for single-line completions; streaming completion startup <120ms for first token; predictable per-developer cost.
Current infra: prototype uses hosted API + local extension web-sockets. Seeing spikes in tail latency during bursts (esp. CI builds + many editors open).
POC plan: 6-week evaluation. Week 1-2: integration + auth (SSO). Week 3-4: latency tuning + model pinning. Week 5: pilot with 100 power users. Week 6: procurement/contracting.
Security: procurement needs SOC2 Type II report and KMS/HSM details. Also asked about audit-logging retention and per-request metadata retention controls.

Model requirements: ability to pin stable model hash for extension releases; automated fallback policy to smaller quantized models when capacity constrained; preference for models with deterministic samplers for reproducible suggestions.
Rate limits: want per-IDE-instance and per-org pooled quotas; also token-budgeting per-session (to avoid runaway token costs during large completions).
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-18): "If we get >40ms median for inline suggestions users will notice lag — can't ship that."
Quote from Head of Product (email): "Need clear rollback plan if model update regresses completions in prod — model pinning + canary required."

Proof-of-concept notes: ran quick bench with Redwood hosted (gpt-small-quant) — median 35ms in us-east, but 99th ~310ms under 150 concurrent sessions. Concerned about 99th tail; requesting dedicated reserved burst pool for predictable tails.

Telemetry/privacy: extension collects contextual file path, language, and last 200 chars of buffer for prompt; legal wants clear telemetry toggles and opt-out. Discussed local KMS for encryption-at-rest for prompts.
Integration items: SSO via SAML 2.0 (Okta), SCIM provisioning, webhook for usage events, extension-level SDK for streaming tokens (we tested streaming with SSE but prefer gRPC-web if supported).

Pricing sensitivity: startup-style pricing for first 12 months helpful; after that expected $5-10 per active-dev/month plus token usage; wants cost simulation from Redwood Optimize for projected 12-month usage.
Docs requested: detailed latency benchmarks (p95/p99) for incremental context sizes, batching behavior, and example quantization tradeoffs for VS Code workloads.
Drive refs: pricing deck shared 2026-03-04; security FAQ updated 2026-03-09.
Next demo scheduled: 2026-03-17 — live walk-through of streaming plugin + canary rollout UI. SE Jordan to run.
Escalations: early support ticket INF-2397 about incorrect rate-limit headers on SSE responses — SE investigating (linked ticket INF-2461 for replication steps).
Procurement timeline: legal review + SOC2 proof needed before procurement — procurement aimed to finish by 2026-04.
Buying signals: CTO asked about signed SLA for latency; engineering asked for test lift to run our synthetic workload on Dedicated pool for 48h.
